visuals: A sunny tropical coastline in Ghana with palm trees and a light afternoon rain shower under a warm sky. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: The climate? Oh, it's warm, tropical, and toasty! Like summer all year round! Ghana usually swings between two main seasons: wet and dry, though some places feel different depending on where you are.

visuals: A wide view of the massive Lake Volta in Ghana with small wooden boats and a green shoreline. No text, no signs, no written words.
script:
Now for my favorite part… nature! Ghana has one of the biggest man-made lakes in the world: Lake Volta!
It’s so huge, it's like a lake that never ends!

visuals: Black Star Square in Accra in Ghana bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Speaking of shining symbols, Ghana doesn’t have an official national animal, but the tawny eagle is admired for its strength as it soars high in the skies.

visuals: An African forest elephant standing in a green forest clearing in Ghana. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Down below, look out for the African forest elephant: quiet, powerful, and usually found roaming through the forests.

visuals: Cheeky monkeys swinging playfully through the lush branches of a Ghanaian forest. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: You'll also spot cheeky monkeys swinging playfully through the trees!

visuals: A busy urban street in Accra, Ghana, with vibrant markets and the modern city skyline near the coast. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Can you guess Ghana’s capital? It’s Accra! A super-busy city with buzzing markets, beachy coastlines, and street food that'll make your nose do a happy dance.

visuals: A Ghanaian artisan weaving traditional kente cloth on a loom in Kumasi, using vibrant colored threads. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: But wait, there's more! Kumasi dazzles with its handmade kente cloth, woven in eye-popping colors.

visuals: A traditional mud house with a thatched roof in Tamale, Ghana, surrounded by lush green trees. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Then there’s Tamale, known for its traditional mud houses and nearby wildlife parks.

visuals: Black Star Square in Accra in Ghana bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: People speak English, but that’s just the start. Many switch easily between languages like Akan, Ewe, or Dagbani, even in the same sentence!

visuals: The vibrant Makola Market in Ghana bustling with people and inhabitants. Open space, not closed. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Ghana is home to around 33 million people! That's about the same number of people living in Texas, USA. Imagine a Texas-sized Ghana!

visuals: A plate of authentic Ghanaian jollof rice served with fried plantains and a fresh side salad. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: On to the tasty stuff… yum! Ever tried jollof rice? It’s a spicy tomato rice dish, perfect for parties and family feasts.

visuals: Soft fufu balls served in a bowl of spicy light soup with pieces of meat, being shared by people in Ghana. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Fufu, often made from cassava, is rolled into soft balls, dipped in soup, and shared with everyone around the table.

visuals: Ripe yellow and red cocoa pods hanging from a tree in a Ghanaian plantation. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And yes, Ghana grows cocoa beans.

visuals: A display of high-quality dark chocolate bars made from Ghanaian cocoa beans. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: That means… chocolate!

visuals: Ghanaian musicians playing guitars and drums for a dancing crowd dressed in bright, traditional kente attire. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Now crank up the music! Highlife is a bouncy, joyful rhythm that fills weddings and street parties with dancing feet. Can't sit still? Me neither!

visuals: People in Ghana celebrating the Homowo Festival with traditional drumming, dancing, and sharing large plates of food. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And get this: the Homowo Festival celebrates a historic harvest and overcoming hunger, with drumming, dancing, and sharing food across families and friends.

visuals: A historic black-and-white image of the 1957 independence parade in Ghana with the national flag waving. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: Back in 1957, Ghana made history by becoming the first African country south of the Sahara to gain independence. That’s a big win for freedom!

visuals: Ghanaian soccer legend Abedi Pelé in his national team jersey on the pitch. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: On the soccer field, watch out for legends like Abedi Pelé.

visuals: Ghanaian soccer player Mohammed Kudus celebrating a goal in a stadium. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And young star Mohammed Kudus.

visuals: The sun setting over the quiet Ghanaian savanna with the sky painted in vibrant orange and purple tones. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: And here’s a kicker: Ghana is close to the equator, so sunrise and sunset happen at almost the same time every day. No daylight savings needed!

visuals: The Greenwich Meridian Line marker in Tema, Ghana, showing the point where the east and west meet. No text, no signs, no written words.
script: One more cool thing: want to stand where the world’s directions meet? Visit the Greenwich Meridian Line in Ghana, where east meets west!
